metadata.title: The Gatekeeper Needs Ground Truth
metadata.purpose: Provenance Gatekeeper development log, Week 2 — the ingestion and retrieval engine: the Intercept Framework, a hand-labeled ground-truth corpus, HuggingFace embeddings into ChromaDB, the n8n/FastAPI intercept, and the directional blind spot semantic search cannot close.

beats.narration_text: I am Onkar Bhujbal, a software engineer. When an AI hallucinates a financial claim, you cannot ask the AI to verify it. You have to intercept the claim and cross-reference it against an immutable ledger. This week, we built the ingestion and retrieval engine to do exactly that.

beats.narration_text: The Provenance Gatekeeper doesn't catch hallucinations with intuition. It catches them with receipts — claims checked against a ledger a human labeled. Week two was about building that ledger.

beats.narration_text: We grade retrieval systems on the Intercept Framework. First, you need hand-labeled ground-truth data. Second, a mathematical representation of that data — the embedding. Third, a webhook that intercepts live claims and performs a similarity search against the vectors.

beats.narration_text: Applying the framework. We built a fifty-row evaluation corpus of financial variance notes. Every row pairs a claim against what the ledger actually says, and a human wrote the label in the last column. Doc oh-one: actual Q3 growth was twelve percent.

beats.narration_text: When our n8n orchestrator fires a webhook to our FastAPI endpoint, the system pulls doc oh-one out of the database and proves the fifteen percent claim is a magnitude error.

beats.narration_text: So where does semantic search break? Directional errors. If the AI claims revenue decreased by twelve percent, but the text says it grew by twelve percent, the vector similarity is nearly identical — the numbers and the topics match perfectly. Retrieval alone isn't enough. The downstream evaluation layer has to calculate the directional polarity.
beats.new_visual_element: The directional blind spot — high similarity, opposite sign

show.event: left card lands: AI CLAIM — 'Q3 revenue decreased 12%'
right card lands: LEDGER doc_01 — 'Actual Q3 growth was 12%'
similarity bar fills almost to full on 'nearly identical' — deliberately unnumbered
'decreased' and 'growth' both light terracotta — the ONLY difference between the two vectors
terracotta verdict block drops: RETRIEVAL ALONE CANNOT CATCH THIS

props.simCaption: near-identical — the metric and the figure both match
props.verdictSub: the evaluation layer must compute directional polarity

beats.honesty_note: The similarity bar carries NO number. The source says the vectors are 'nearly identical' and publishes no cosine figure, so none is shown (DOUBLE-CHECK LAW).

beats.narration_text: So test your own database. Send this exact JSON payload to your local verify endpoint. If ChromaDB does not return the exact ground-truth ledger line, your embedding model is misaligned.
beats.new_visual_element: The JSON payload the viewer POSTs to /verify

the JSON payload reveals line by line as the voice reads the instruction
TASK line lands under the block: POST to /verify

props.title: payload.json
props.code:
{
  "claim_id": "test_1",
  "generated_claim": "Q3 Revenue increased 15%"
}

# TASK: POST to /verify
#
# Expected: ChromaDB returns doc_01 —
#   "Actual Q3 growth was 12%"  ·  MAGNITUDE
#
# Anything else and your embedding model is misaligned.

beats.narration_text: And when it comes back wrong, here is the prompt worth running. Take the twenty claims your own tooling produced this week, write the ground-truth line that would settle each one, then label the gap — magnitude, directional, or causal. Then name the class you have no ground truth for at all. That last answer is the one that matters. The class you cannot label is the class your verifier will never catch.

props.command: Take the 20 factual claims my tooling produced this week. For each, write the ground-truth line that would settle it, then label the gap: magnitude, directional, or causal. Then tell me which claim type I have no ground truth for at all.

beats.narration_text: High-quality, ground-truth data is the absolute foundation of any reliable AI verification engine. Onkar Bhujbal, for Humanitarians AI.
